name: Carl Lambrecht
bio: Carl Lambrecht is a Highland Park optical engineer who has owned the optics manufacturer Laurel Industries since 1978 and holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Illinois. He was the Republican nominee for Illinois House District 58 in 2024, losing to incumbent Bob Morgan, and is the Republican nominee against Rep. Brad Schneider in 2026.

platform.point: Proposed cutting the Illinois gas tax in half and reducing the number of taxing bodies, including school districts.
Opposed state money for a Chinese-owned battery factory and the $7,500 incentive for electric car buyers.
Said fighting corruption starts with officials who believe in God and the Ten Commandments.
Names the cost of public services as the top local issue and says his work abroad shows how to lower it.

economy.evidence: In a 2024 questionnaire he proposed halving the state gas tax, cutting the number of taxing bodies and ending subsidies for a battery plant and EV buyers.

energy.evidence: Called for ending the $7,500 electric vehicle purchase incentive and state support for a battery factory.

faith.evidence: Answered questions on corruption and redistricting by saying officials should believe in God and follow the Ten Commandments.

notes: Positions come from his 2024 Sun-Times questionnaire for Illinois House District 58 (the district the first pass could not confirm); no campaign website was found, Vote-USA lists no answers and the Daily Herald questionnaire did not load. Positions on welfare, immigration, foreign policy, social issues, tech and education remain unknown.

name: Julie Fortier
bio: Julie Fortier is a U.S. Air Force veteran of Desert Shield who served four years as an enlisted member, and a research pathologist with a Ph.D. in biomedical science who has worked on multiple myeloma research. A longtime O'Fallon resident and first-time candidate, she is the Democratic nominee against Rep. Mike Bost in Illinois's 12th district.

platform.point: Supports moving gradually toward universal health care, starting by restoring ACA subsidies.
Backs a higher federal minimum wage and closing corporate tax loopholes, and rejects trickle-down economics.
Says abortion decisions belong to a woman and her doctor and opposes federal restrictions.
Supports Second Amendment rights along with background checks before gun purchases.
Opposes the Medicaid and ACA subsidy cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, citing rural hospitals.
Opposes the current tariff approach and the Argentina beef deal as harmful to Illinois farmers.
Proposes expanding the Court to 13 justices, with term limits and enforceable ethics rules.
Says her campaign refuses corporate PAC and AIPAC money.

economy.evidence: Supports raising the federal minimum wage and closing corporate tax loopholes, and rejects trickle-down economics.

welfare.evidence: Calls for universal health care phased in over time, beginning with restored ACA subsidies, and opposes Medicaid cuts.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: says the decision belongs to a woman and her doctor; guns: backs the Second Amendment with background checks; speech: proposed fines for news outlets that knowingly air falsehoods.

energy.evidence: General statement that climate change requires immediate action to protect younger generations.

notes: Found her campaign site plus Illinois Public Media, Daily Egyptian and Southern Illinois Now interviews; the WTTW guide blocked automated access and the site's priorities page returned 404. No public positions found on immigration, foreign policy, policing, tech, education or religion.

name: Dillan Vancil
current_role: Small-business owner and rail union legislative director
bio: Dillan Vancil, 33, is a former locomotive engineer from the Monmouth area who has served as Illinois state legislative director for the SMART-TD rail union and co-founded the Dame Fine Coffee drive-through chain. He has served on the West Central school board, including as vice president, and on the Eagle View health system board, and won the March 2026 Republican primary to face Rep. Eric Sorensen.

platform.point: Top priority is expanding American energy by easing coal limits, growing natural gas and investing in nuclear power.
Would exempt the first $25,000 of individual income ($50,000 for couples) from federal income tax.
Wants lower prices through price transparency, competition and limits on hospital and insurance middlemen rather than federal mandates.
Opposes illegal immigration but wants easier legal entry for skilled workers and investors with jobs or investments lined up.
Backs the administration's trade pressure on China but wants trade policy fixed so farmers do not need bailouts.
Supports changes to keep Social Security and Medicare solvent, focusing on fraud and growth over across-the-board cuts.
Wants to bring manufacturing jobs back to Illinois and support small businesses.
Aims to secure student funding and education access for rural communities.

economy.evidence: Proposes exempting the first $25,000 of income from federal income tax and deregulating energy, while also supporting tariffs as a negotiating tool.

welfare.evidence: Prefers competition and more plan options over federal health mandates, and would target fraud to keep Social Security and Medicare solvent.

immigration.evidence: Opposes illegal immigration and calls for serious border security, but wants legal immigration made easier for skilled workers and investors.

foreign.evidence: Opposes open-ended aid to Ukraine or Israel while the U.S. border is insecure and supports only narrowly focused actions tied to core U.S. interests.

energy.evidence: Wants to reverse limits on coal, expand natural gas and invest in nuclear power to lower energy costs.

tech.evidence: Opposes heavy AI regulation, saying Congress should clear barriers so U.S. companies can out-innovate China.

notes: Scores come from his 2026 Shaw Local questionnaire and campaign site; WQAD, MyStateline and WTTW pages blocked automated access. Abortion and gun positions appeared only in a supporter's letter, not his own words, so liberty, security, education and faith remain unscored.

name: Lupe Castillo
bio: Lupe Castillo was born in San Antonio, has lived in Illinois's 4th district for more than 40 years and has worked as a chef and in the pharmacy industry. A former 22nd Ward Republican committeewoman, she was the Republican nominee for this seat in 2024 and is again in 2026.

platform.point: Called for closing the border and restoring the Remain in Mexico policy.
Supports a balanced budget amendment, a 15% corporate tax rate and Sen. Rand Paul's Penny Plan.
Opposes taxing tips and overtime.
Backed reviving an oil pipeline and expanding offshore drilling to boost the economy.
Supports school choice so low-income families have options.
Supports voter ID requirements, citing fraud concerns in Chicago.
Wants girls' sports and bathrooms limited to biological females and opposes surgeries for minors without parental consent.
Backed firm support for Ukraine with auditable aid, and military aid to Israel alongside humanitarian aid for Palestinians.

economy.evidence: Supports a balanced budget amendment, cutting the corporate tax rate to 15%, ending taxes on tips and overtime, and the Penny Plan spending cuts.

liberty.evidence: Guns: a lifetime NRA and Gun Owners of America member; LGBTQ: wants girls' sports and bathrooms limited to biological females and opposes surgeries for minors without parental consent.

security.evidence: General statement backing police and pledging to reverse what she calls pro-criminal policies.

immigration.evidence: Called for closing the border, restoring Remain in Mexico and removing incentives for illegal entry.

foreign.evidence: Said U.S. support for Ukraine should be unwavering, with auditable aid and fair NATO burden-sharing, and backed military aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Proposed reinstating an oil pipeline and expanding offshore drilling.

education.evidence: Campaign site backs school choice so low-income families can choose schools.

notes: Found her 2026 campaign site (home and values pages) and her October 2024 Sun-Times questionnaire for the same seat, which supplies the immigration, foreign, energy and tax answers. No public positions found on welfare programs, tech regulation or religion in public life.

name: Chad Koppie
bio: Chad Koppie is a northern Illinois farmer and a retired Delta Air Lines captain who trained at Purdue University's aviation school. He has served on the Kane County Regional Board of School Trustees since 2007, including three terms as president, and earlier on the District 300 school board and as a Rutland Township trustee. A frequent candidate for federal and statewide office, he won the March 2026 Republican primary for the open 7th district seat.

platform.point: Names ending abortion as his main goal and backs a constitutional amendment defining life as beginning at conception.
Would cut spending in every federal department by 3% a year, with matching tax cuts, and abolish the Federal Reserve.
Build a border wall and have ICE arrest and deport all people in the country illegally.
Pledges never to vote for gun control and to defend the right of law-abiding citizens to own guns.
Proposes a seasonal ceasefire in Ukraine so grain and fertilizer exports can resume.
Calls for abolishing the IRS and the U.S. Department of Education and repealing the Affordable Care Act.
Called for repealing Illinois' SAFE-T Act and holding violent offenders accountable.
Would restrict driver's licenses and credit cards of parents who fall behind on child support.

economy.evidence: Proposes 3% annual cuts across all federal agencies with tax cuts, and abolishing the Federal Reserve and the IRS.

welfare.evidence: Calls for repealing the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: backs a constitutional amendment that life begins at conception; LGBTQ: supports protecting traditional marriage; guns: pledges never to vote for gun control.

security.evidence: Called for repealing Illinois' SAFE-T Act criminal justice law and strengthening law enforcement against violent offenders.

immigration.evidence: Supports a border wall and ICE arrest and deportation of all people in the country illegally, and opposes sanctuary policies.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending all foreign aid.

education.evidence: Calls for eliminating the U.S. Department of Education.

notes: Added positions from his campaign issues page, CBS Chicago's 2026 primary guide and Block Club Chicago forum coverage; the SAFE-T Act point comes from search-result text because Block Club rate-limited the fetch. No stated positions found on energy, tech regulation or religion in public life.

name: Barb Regnitz
bio: Barb Regnitz is a Porter County commissioner from Valparaiso who won the Republican nomination for Indiana's 1st district in May 2026 with about 46% of the vote. She holds Purdue degrees in mathematics and German, worked as a software engineer, project manager and certified financial planner, and has served on the boards of the Valparaiso Rotary Club, the Rotary Foundation and SCORE.

platform.point: Supports law enforcement and wants to end catch-and-release practices that return offenders to the street.
Wants stronger border security and immigration rules that prioritize safety and legal entry.
Wants to curb spending and inflation, cut waste and fraud, and reduce the national debt.
Backs same-day in-person voting on watermarked paper ballots, with mail-in voting only in rare verified cases.
Wants schools to focus on teaching students how to think rather than what to think.
Supports reserving girls' sports and facilities for biological females.
Defends the right to bear arms and favors enforcing existing laws against violent criminals over new limits on legal owners.
Wants to address harmful food additives, working alongside RFK Jr. and the Trump administration.

economy.evidence: General statement: platform calls for cutting wasteful federal spending and reducing the national debt.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: wants girls' sports and facilities limited to biological females; guns: opposes new restrictions on law-abiding owners.

security.evidence: General statement backing more resources for police and an end to catch-and-release of criminal offenders.

immigration.evidence: General statement calling for stronger border security and immigration rules focused on safety and legal entry.

tech.evidence: General statement under a financial-freedom plank supporting innovation without overregulation.

notes: Read the full eight-plank platform from the campaign site's page code; the catch-and-release plank concerns criminal offenders, so the immigration score was lowered to reflect only a general border statement. No positions found on welfare, foreign policy, energy, school choice or religion; nwitimes and Fox59 blocked automated access.

name: Patrick McAuley
bio: Patrick McAuley, 29, is a lifelong Indianapolis resident who works in commercial real estate and is the Republican nominee for Indiana's 7th district against Rep. André Carson. A North Central High School graduate, he was an athlete at Wabash College, earned a master's degree in international economics and finance, and has interned in the U.S. Senate.

platform.point: Wants stronger community-police relationships, more officers in neighborhoods and targeted crime-reduction resources.
Proposes expanding housing supply and reusing vacant buildings to address rising rents.
Supports partnerships and federal resources to help people move off the street.
Proposes a 10-15% increase in federal funding for registered apprenticeships in the skilled trades.
Wants to restore federal road funding he says Indiana lost last year.
Proposes a congressional caucus to keep communities informed about data center decisions.
Promotes a 10-point affordability agenda aimed at gas, housing and prescription drug costs.

economy.evidence: Proposes raising federal apprenticeship funding by 10-15% and restoring federal road money, framing his run around bringing federal resources to the district.

security.evidence: Calls for increasing police officer presence in neighborhoods alongside community policing.

notes: Checked his campaign pages, Mirror Indy, WFYI, WIBC and Butler Collegian coverage; iVoterGuide shows no answers and the Indianapolis Recorder Q&A blocked access. Search snippets attributed immigration, health care and abortion quotes to him but no readable source confirmed them, so those topics stay unscored.

name: Don Coover
bio: Don Coover grew up on a family farm in rural southeast Kansas, graduated from West Point and served more than ten years as a U.S. Army officer, including as an infantry officer and Army aviator. A Kansas State University veterinary graduate, he runs a cattle genetics company, a working ranch near Galesburg and a livestock veterinary practice. He has not held elected office and faces Rep. Derek Schmidt.

platform.point: Focus on bringing down grocery, housing and health care costs for working families.
Wants more federal investment and protected Medicare funding to keep rural Kansas hospitals open.
Opposes the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, saying it shifted the tax burden away from the wealthy and added to the debt.
Says current tariffs are harming Kansas agriculture.
Wants to end insider trading by politicians and no-bid government contracts.
Treat farm policy as central to food prices and grocery bills.
Reduce partisan gridlock and have Washington spend within its means.

economy.evidence: Opposes the One Big Beautiful Bill Act for shifting the tax burden away from the wealthy, while also criticizing tariffs and the added debt.

welfare.evidence: General statement supporting protected Medicare and more federal investment in rural hospitals, and health care that puts patients ahead of insurer profits.

notes: Reviewed his campaign site (no issues page) plus Kansas Public Radio and Kansas Reflector coverage; KSN and the Reflector's own site blocked automated access. No public positions found on social issues, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech, education or religion.
